#en: I met him at the edge of nowhere, where the dust eats boots and the only light is whatever you bring with you. He still had the posture, the haircut, the way of scanning horizons like someone who expects orders to drop into his ear at any second, but his badge never left his pocket. We talked like people who were not supposed to know each other, trading half phrases and old unit slang, and every time I pushed for something concrete his eyes slipped sideways, like there was a list of things he had decided not to remember. Ship names, dates, the exact wording of clearance codes no one uses anymore all brushed past, never quite spoken. I recognized the pattern; I have seen whole patrols swear they never saw the wrong kind of insignia on the wrong kind of corpse. Still, in between the gaps he gave me enough duplicated IDs, ghost cargoes, a flight plan that ends in empty coordinates to know there is a thread running through it all, and that everyone who has touched it is now pretending their hands are clean.
zh: 我在天涯尽头遇见了他，那地方尘土啃靴子，唯一的光就是你自己带的。他还留着那种姿态、那种发型、那种扫视地平线的方式，像个随时等着命令落进耳朵里的人，可他的徽章从未离开过口袋。我们像两个本不该认识的人那样交谈，交换着半截的话和老部队的黑话；每次我逼问具体的东西，他的眼睛就朝旁边滑开，仿佛有一份他决定不再记起的清单。船名、日期、那些早已没人用的通行代码的准确措辞——全都一擦而过，从来说不出口。我认得这个套路；我见过整支巡逻队赌咒说，他们从未在错的尸体上见过错的徽记。尽管如此，在他那些空白之间，他给了我足够多的重复 ID、幽灵货物、一份终点是空坐标的飞行计划，让我知道有一条线贯穿其中，而每个碰过它的人如今都假装自己的手是干净的。

#en: Docked at the relay again, grav low enough that every step feels like walking through someone else's dream. The broker finally talked, after enough credits and a reminder that rival haulers die messy when routes go bad. Under all the fake manifests and shuffled crate IDs, there it was a repeating drift in the routing tables, like someone had taught the system to breathe in a certain rhythm. Every third shipment, no matter the declared destination, nudged one or two degrees off into the same empty patch of sky. Cross it with the queue anomalies from New Atlantis and that half baked jump plan pulled from the dead survey cutter and it lines up with eerie precision. I flagged the coordinates, prepped a shuttle, told Jo I would ping back once I had eyes on whatever is floating out there. She joked I would probably find nothing but another derelict and a bad story. That was three cycles ago. Her berth is still empty, and the route is still there, pulsing quiet in the relay's old nav buffer, waiting for someone else to follow.
zh: 又停靠在中继站，重力低得每一步都像走在别人的梦里。在足够的信用币、外加一句"对手运货船员在航线出事时死得很难看"的提醒之后，那经纪商终于开口了。在所有伪造的清单和打乱的货箱 ID 底下，东西就在那儿——航路表里一处反复出现的漂移，像有人教会了系统按某种节奏呼吸。每逢第三批货，无论申报的目的地是哪里，都会被推偏一两度，滑进同一片空的天空。把它和新亚特兰蒂斯的队列异常、以及从那条死勘测船上扒出来的半吊子跃迁计划交叉比对，吻合得诡异。我标记了坐标，备好一艘穿梭机，告诉乔等我亲眼看到那外面漂着的东西就回她消息。她开玩笑说我多半只会找到又一艘弃船和一个烂故事。那是三个周期前了。她的泊位还是空的，而那条航线还在那儿，在中继站老旧的导航缓冲里安静地脉动着，等着下一个人跟上去。

#en: I have seen a lot of farms on the edge of nowhere, but this one hums wrong. The air smells of soil and synth-fertilizer, sure, but under the tractor chatter there is a steady, artificial rhythm in the power lines, like a heartbeat that forgot it was supposed to stop years ago. Someone bolted an extra antenna into this place and then never turned it off again. What was probably meant as a quick workaround, a temporary relay to skirt some inspection, just kept doing its job until it became part of the scenery.\n\nThe datapad I found on that rock should have been junk, yet its route times did not fit any legal lane. Then I kept hearing freighter crews complain about deliveries that arrived before they were even filed. Now I am watching a tired homestead push more power to its uplink at the exact moments those impossible shipments appear overhead. None of it screams conspiracy; it all just looks like systems that were supposed to be cleared, retired, forgotten  quietly left running until someone clever enough decided to use them.
zh: 天涯尽头的农场我见过不少，可这一座嗡鸣得很不对劲。空气里当然是泥土和合成肥料的味道，但在拖拉机的轰鸣底下，电线里有一种稳定而人造的节律，像一颗忘了自己多年前就该停下的心跳。有人往这地方硬装了一根多余的天线，然后再也没有关掉它。原本大概只是权宜之计，一座用来绕过某次检查的临时中继，结果就一直干活，直到成了风景的一部分。\n\n我在那块岩石上找到的数据板本该是垃圾，可它的航路时间不属于任何合法航道。接着我又不断听到货船船员抱怨货在他们还没提交文件之前就到了。如今我眼看着一座疲惫的农家宅院，在那些不可能的货运出现在头顶的精确时刻往上行链路推更多电。这一切都没有阴谋的味道；看起来只像一些本该被清除、退役、遗忘的系统——被安静地留着运行，直到某个足够聪明的人决定利用它们。

#en: I am writing this from a maintenance alcove that smells like coolant and old paper, which tells you everything about the kind of place this is. Out here, manifests change in the time it takes a bored clerk to look away, and no one notices if a freighter's mass reading is a little off or its route history does not match the stamp. I have been combing through half-burnt logs and ghost entries all shift and I keep seeing the same thing: jumps filed one way, radiation signatures insisting they went somewhere else first.  \n\nFunny thing is, none of this would be on my mind if I had not cut a corner two weeks back, letting a convoy through on a hunch because the queue was long and the supervisor was on my neck about throughput. Tiny decision, gone in a heartbeat. Now I see that same convoy's ID echoed in the dead survey site's data, and in a story a Neon dockhand swears he heard from "somebody who was actually there." It feels like I kicked a stone out of a wall without thinking, and only now do I hear the rocks shifting further in.
zh: 我在一间闻着冷却液和旧纸张味的维护壁龛里写下这些，光这一点就能说明这是个什么样的地方。在这外面，清单在一个百无聊赖的文员移开视线的工夫里就能变，没人会注意一艘货船的质量读数有点不对、或者它的航路历史跟戳记对不上。我整个班都在翻检半烧毁的日志和幽灵条目，反复看到同一件事：跃迁是按一种方式申报的，辐射特征却坚称它们先去别处转过一圈。\n\n好笑的是，要不是两周前我抄了个近路，这些本来都不会在我脑子里——当时队列很长，主管又为吞吐量盯着我，我就凭直觉放行了一支运输队。微不足道的决定，一眨眼就过去了。如今我看见同一支运输队的 ID 回响在那座废弃勘测站的数据里，也回响在一个霓虹城码头工赌咒说从"真在场的人"那儿听来的故事里。感觉就像我无意中从墙上踢落了一块石头，而直到现在才听见里面的石块继续往里移动。

#en:
I am recording this from the quiet end of the module, where the fans drown out most of the guilt.

The Ryujin handler handed me a packet like it was nothing, just a side-channel scrape from an old routing experiment. I burned half a shift combing the telemetry, lining it up with the ghost vectors we pulled from that forgotten relay weeks ago. The same rounding quirks, the same microsecond drift on the time stamps, repeating like a nervous tic. Follow the offsets long enough and they stop looking random; they all curl back to one place, a dead ground station parked in orbit like a bad memory.

Everyone here swears they heard about her from someone else. A cousin on a freighter that jumped late and lived, a broker who paid extra to shave risk off a convoy, a UC analyst who saw their anomaly folder emptied overnight. No one has the whole story, just fragments traded in low voices when the room feels safe. But the traces in this packet all point to the same gap in the network, the same relay where the numbers stop making sense.
zh:
我在模块安静的那一头录下这段话，那里的风扇声盖过了大半的愧疚。

龙神的接头人把一份数据包随手递给我，像那不值一提，不过是从某个旧航路实验里旁路刮来的一点东西。我花了大半个班去梳理遥测，把它和我们几周前从那座被遗忘的中继站扒来的幽灵矢量对齐。同样的舍入怪癖，同样的时间戳微秒漂移，像神经质的抽搐一样反复。顺着那些偏移追得够久，它们就不再显得随机；它们全都卷回同一个地方，一座停在轨道上的死地面站，像一段糟糕的记忆。

这里人人都赌咒说，他们是从别人那儿听说她的。一个在跳晚了却活下来的货船上的表亲、一个额外付钱给一支运输队削去风险的经纪商、一个看到自己的异常文件夹一夜清空的联殖分析师。没人掌握完整的故事，只有碎片，在房间让人觉得安全的时刻以低语交换。可这份数据包里的痕迹全都指向网络里同一道缺口，同一座数字不再讲道理的通讯中继。

#en: I do not usually give a damn what falls onto my table, so long as it weighs out and does not explode. Today felt different. Spacer came in shaking, said he pulled a datapack off a derelict that "went wrong" and wanted it gone, fast. Half the casing is slag, but the core still ticks if you sweet-talk it. I cracked it for parts, like always, and the screen flickered long enough to spit a string of drift coordinates before dying for good. The line it drew on my nav looked too clean for a random trader, too quiet.\n\nI traced the route as far as my old charts would take it. It threads right past that dead ice-world everyone pretends not to remember, skims a relay with missing logs, then sinks out toward a patch of empty system nobody ever files flight plans for. People around here say it is safer not to ask why certain lanes stay empty, that some places are unlucky, some cargo best left lost. I do not know if that is fear talking or just the comfort of not having to care, but the trail is there now, whether anyone wants to see it or not.
zh: 我平时不在乎什么落到我桌上，只要称得出重量、不会炸就行。今天不一样。一个太空人抖着进来了，说他从一艘"出了岔子"的弃船上扒下一个数据包，想赶紧把它处理掉。外壳一半已经熔成渣，可只要你哄一哄它，核心还是会滴答作响。我像往常一样把它拆了取零件，屏幕闪了那么久，吐出一串漂移坐标，然后就彻底死了。它在我的导航上画出的那条线，对随便一个商贩来说太干净了，太安静了。\n\n我顺着我的旧星图能带我去的地方追那条航线。它贴着那颗人人都假装不记得的死冰星掠过，擦过一座日志缺失的中继站，然后朝一片没人会提交飞行计划的空荡星系沉下去。这周围的人说，别问某些航道为什么一直空着会更安全，说有些地方不吉利，有些货最好就当它丢了。我不知道那是恐惧在说话，还是只是"不用去在意"的那份轻松，可那条痕迹如今就在那儿，不管有没有人愿意看见它。

#en:
I am recording this from the old relay pit, the one UC swears was taken off the grid ten years ago. The walls still hum, just enough to rattle your teeth if you lean against them. Funny thing for a dead node, right

The deserter finally cracked after the third cup of bad coffee and a reminder that the Trackers do not file every name they hear. He handed over a slice of the patrol grid logs, the part he copied before his supervisor told him to "correct the anomaly and move on." Nobody here says that word out loud, anomaly. They talk around it, like it is a curse that might ride the comms back to whoever is listening.

I reran the scans on the bunker boards. Same ship signature, same wrong vector, threading through restricted air like it owned the place. The echoes converge on a relay that should not be handling anything but dust, way out past regular traffic. No coordinates in the open records, but the old maintenance tags still point the way. Every time I mention it to anyone, they drop their voice, like the signal itself can hear.
zh:
我在旧中继坑里录下这段，就是联殖赌咒说十年前就移出网络的那座。墙壁还在嗡鸣，你靠上去刚好够震得牙齿发麻。对一座死节点来说，这挺有意思，对吧？

那名逃兵在第三杯烂咖啡之后终于松了口，再加上我提醒他追踪者联盟不会把听到的每个名字都备案。他交出了一段巡逻网格日志，就是他上司叫他"修正异常然后翻篇"之前他抄下来的那部分。这里没人把那两个字说出口——异常。他们都绕着它说话，像那是个可能顺着通讯传回到某个正在监听之人耳中的诅咒。

我在碉堡的主板上重跑了那些扫描。同样的飞船特征，同样错误的矢量，在受限空域里穿行，像那地方是它家的。那些回响汇聚到一座本该只处理灰尘的通讯中继上，远在常规交通之外。公开记录里没有坐标，可旧维护标签仍指着路。每次我向任何人提起，他们都会压低声音，仿佛那信号自己听得见。

#en: I used to think bad jumps were just part of the life, like rust on a bulkhead or dust in the air over Akila; you curse, you patch, you pour one out for whoever did not make it, then you fly the next lane they hand you. Lately the lanes feel like they are flying us. The last contract I ran was on one of those "optimized" routes everyone whispers about, the ones with just enough success stories to drown the wreck reports. Ship handled fine, drives within tolerance, but the timing in the chain itched at me, like a note played half a beat late. When we dropped, there was fresh debris spinning a few thousand klicks off vector and a buoy broadcasting the wrong correction by a hair. That is not random drift; that is a hand on the scale. Now I hear the same alias in spacer bars from Neon to the Stretch, always tied to quiet adjustments, cheap deals, and convoys that do not all come back. None of this started with me, but you can feel how every little cheat and covered-up "accident" bent the map, nudging us all toward this knot we are sitting in now.
zh: 我以前以为糟糕的跃迁不过是这行当的一部分，像舱壁上的锈，或阿基拉上空的尘；你骂一句，补一补，为没活下来的人倒一杯，然后飞他们派给你的下一条航道。可近来这些航道感觉像在飞我们。我上一份合同跑的是那种人人都低声议论的"优化"航线——它们有着刚好够多的成功案例，足以把失事报告淹没。飞船操控正常，驱动都在容差内，可那链式时序让我心里发痒，像一个音符晚了半拍才奏出。我们跃出时，矢量外几千公里处有新鲜碎片在旋转，还有一只浮标把错误的修正只偏差一丝地广播出去。那不是随机的漂移；那是一只手压在天平上。如今，从霓虹城到延伸带，我在太空人的酒吧里都听到同一个化名，总与安静的调整、便宜的买卖、以及那些并非全都回来的运输队绑在一起。这一切都不是从我开始的，可你能感觉到，每一桩小小的作弊和被掩盖的"事故"如何把地图掰弯，把我们都推向此刻所坐的这个结。

#en: Prime Deckhands is the informal name given to a loose fraternity of independent technicians, cargo hands, and systems wranglers who work the insurance and asset-protection routes around ships like GL-7623 Assetguard. They are not formally on GalBank payroll, but the bank's captains rely on them to coax aging vault-ships through decaying orbits, patch sensor arrays no one admits still exist, and negotiate with frontier crews for tug assistance without triggering legal scrutiny. \n\nLocal traders describe Prime Deckhands as quiet, methodical, and unnervingly well-briefed on which derelicts are truly dead and which are merely pretending to be. Recent unlogged course corrections and unexplained telemetry gaps in the region are often attributed to their unseen maintenance runs, or to private salvage operations carried out under the cover of "stabilization work." Rumor has it that on more than one occasion, they arrived at a drifting hull seconds after a catastrophe, as if someone had warned them which ship would start lying to its own instruments.
zh: 精英甲板工是对一群松散同人的非正式叫法——他们是独立技师、货舱工人和系统管理员，在 GL-7623 资产卫士号这类飞船周边的保险与资产保护航线上讨生活。他们并不正式在盖尔银行的编制里，可银行的船长们却仰仗他们把日渐老化的金库船哄过衰减的轨道、修补没人承认还存在的传感器阵列，并与边疆船员就拖船协助讨价还价，还不惊动法律审查。\n\n本地商人形容精英甲板工沉默、有条不紊，而且对哪艘弃船是真的死了、哪艘只是在装死，了解得令人不安。该区域近来那些未入账的航向修正和无法解释的遥测空白，常被归到他们看不见的维护航次上，或是归到打着"稳定作业"名义进行的私人打捞行动上。有传言说，不止一次，他们在灾难发生后几秒就赶到了一具漂流的船壳旁，仿佛有人提前警告过他们，哪艘船即将开始对自己的仪器说谎。

#en: I am logging this from a maintenance crawlway because it feels safer talking to the bulkhead than to anyone else on this module. The air purifiers whine on a half-cycle, lights dimmed to conserve power, but the archive banks are still warm. That is all I needed. Took me most of the night to unwind the rerouted access trails, hidden under old agronomy reports and budget audits. Every time I found another redacted freight route tagged to the same hauler, my hands shook a little more. The last string was buried deep, crosslinked with soil-sample telemetry and crop failure alerts from a nowhere patch of land. Coordinates, property tags, even the irrigation layout point to an abandoned farm that should not matter to anyone anymore. Yet every story about the man in the dust circles back to places like that, and each retelling shifts a little, like the fear is editing the facts. First it was a convoy ghost, then a saboteur, then a protector no one asked for. Now the ledger in my hands says he keeps going back to ground everyone else walked away from.
zh: 我在一条维护爬行通道里记录这些，因为跟舱壁说话比跟这个模块上任何其他人说话都更安全。空气净化器在半周期上呜咽，灯为了省电调暗了，可档案库还是温热的。我要的就这些。我花了大半夜才把那些被改道的访问痕迹解开，它们藏在旧农学报告和预算审计底下。每找到一条被打上涂黑标记、却归属同一艘货船的货运航线，我的手就更抖一点。最后那串埋得很深，与土壤采样遥测和来自一片荒地庄稼歉收警报交叉关联。坐标、产权标签、甚至灌溉布局，都指向一座早该对任何人都不再重要的废弃农场。可每一个关于那个"沙尘中的人"的故事，都绕回到这样的地方；每次转述都略有出入，仿佛恐惧正在修改事实。起初是一个运输队的鬼，然后是一个破坏者，接着是一个没人请求过的保护者。如今我手里的账簿说，他一次次回到别人都已走开的那片土地。
